why: The two statements differ in kind. A (proposition_18_4_3, universe 0) is an existence statement in a model: for a covering family c and a smooth w over a smooth point of X_Ψ with Γ̄(w) ≅ e, SOME Λ is an sc⁺-multisection functor with Λ(e) > 0, Γ̄^*Λ atomic in the model of c, structurable; exists_atomicData and proposition_18_4_3_formula describe that Λ through a natural representation of G_x in the model. B asserts these properties for the explicit function lam of p. 854, built in one strong bundle uniformizer Ψ̄ from a given local sc⁺-section s and every sc-smooth bump β : O → [0,1] with small support, plus independence of the choice of (q, φ) and atomicity in the model of every family c ⊔ {Ψ̄}. A_to_B would need the whole proof for lam (A says nothing about that function). B_to_A would need, from the model data, a uniformizer with a local sc⁺-section through e and a bump on O (A's bump hypothesis is stated in a model), the hypothesis HasStrongBundleUniformizers that A does not assume, atomicity in the model of c rather than c ⊔ {Ψ̄}, and the AtomicData conjuncts, about which B is silent. Both directions are believed to hold mathematically; each would re-prove substantial parts of §13.5/§17, so neither was attempted.
overlap: No direction proved, so no #rt_check/#rt_overlap; the file records A and A_holds only. B_to_A could be obtained vacuously by copying the project's proofs of all four conjuncts, which would not compare anything and was not done.
